sentences.en: The year is 1924.

sentences.en: My main guy, my guy, Moses Sean Finkel, real sad story.
sentences.zh: 我的偶像，我的老兄，摩西·申芬克尔，一个非常悲伤的故事。

sentences.zh: 但在那之前，他设法独立发表了一篇论文，另一篇是与人合著的。

sentences.en: And that one paper was called On the Building Blocks of Mathematical Logic.
sentences.zh: 那篇论文叫《论数理逻辑的基石》。

sentences.en: And my guy, Moses, Sean Finkel, introduces five combinators, I, C, and S, two others that don't really matter, T and Z, but C would later be renamed the K combinator.
sentences.zh: 我的老兄摩西·申芬克尔引入了五个组合子：I、C 和 S，还有两个不太重要的，T 和 Z，但 C 后来被重命名为 K 组合子。

sentences.en: And I, K, and S, for those of you that are in the know, are the three combinators that make up the S-K-I combinator calculus.
sentences.zh: 对于知情者来说，I、K 和 S 是构成 S-K-I 组合子演算的三个组合子。

sentences.en: We'll get to that in a sec.
sentences.zh: 我们一会儿就会讲到。

sentences.en: This is in 1924.
sentences.zh: 这是在 1924 年。

sentences.en: Five years later, a guy named Haskell Curry, some of you may or may not have heard of him.
sentences.zh: 五年后，一个叫哈斯克尔·柯里的家伙出现了，你们有些人可能听说过他，也可能没听说过。

sentences.en: The Haskell is from Haskell, and the Curry is from Curry.
sentences.zh: Haskell 语言的 Haskell 就是取自他，Curry 语言的 Curry 也是取自他。

sentences.en: No big deal.
sentences.zh: 没什么大不了的。

sentences.en: He rediscovers combinatory logic and also discovers that Sean Finkel had this paper in 24 that introduces these combinators.
sentences.zh: 他重新发现了组合子逻辑，也发现了申芬克尔在 24 年发表的那篇引入这些组合子的论文。

sentences.en: So his paper, I believe, is called An Analysis of Substitution Logic or something like that.
sentences.zh: 所以他的论文，我想是叫《代换逻辑分析》之类的。

sentences.en: And that is one of his first papers that will lead to two or three decades of research on what ultimately is going to be called
sentences.zh: 那是他最早的论文之一，随后引发了二三十年的研究，最终被称为

sentences.en: Combinatory Logic.
sentences.zh: 组合子逻辑。

sentences.en: And he publishes, Haskell Curry, that is, publishes a seminal text, which is volume one of a two-volume book, textbook with, I believe the first volume is
sentences.zh: 哈斯克尔·柯里出版了一本开创性的著作，这是一本两卷本教科书的第一卷，我想第一卷是

sentences.en: authored with Robert Faze, who I actually don't know who that is, but co-authors should get mentioned.
sentences.zh: 与罗伯特·费兹合著的，我其实不知道他是谁，但合著者应该被提及。

sentences.en: And this is basically, it's an untyped, simple lambda calculus.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是一个无类型的简单 lambda 演算。

sentences.en: So everyone's heard of lambda calculus, but like, at least to me, a lot less people have heard of this S-K-I combinator calculus or combinatory logic.
sentences.zh: 所以每个人都听说过 lambda 演算，但对我来说，听说过这种 S-K-I 组合子演算或组合子逻辑的人要少得多。

sentences.en: And all you actually need to have a Turing complete language is S and K.
sentences.zh: 而要拥有一个图灵完备的语言，你实际上只需要 S 和 K。

sentences.en: I is expressible in terms of S and K.
sentences.zh: I 可以用 S 和 K 来表示。

sentences.en: But, but, okay, but hang on, hang on, hang on.
sentences.zh: 但是，但是，好吧，等等，等等，等等。

sentences.en: What is a combinator?
sentences.zh: 什么是组合子？

sentences.en: A combinator, in my, in my opinion, is a composition pattern.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，组合子是一种组合模式。

sentences.en: They're all just functions, higher order functions.
sentences.zh: 它们本质上都是函数，高阶函数。

sentences.en: Some of them don't really express, quote unquote, composition patterns, such as the I combinator, because the I combinator is just the identity function.
sentences.zh: 其中一些并没有真正表达所谓的“组合模式”，比如 I 组合子，因为 I 组合子只是恒等函数。

sentences.en: For those of you that have not heard of the identity function, it's a function that takes a single argument and returns you back that argument.
sentences.zh: 对于那些没听说过恒等函数的人，它就是一个接收单个参数并原样返回该参数的函数。

sentences.en: When I first heard of the identity function, I thought, that sounds stupid.
sentences.zh: 当我第一次听说恒等函数时，我想，这听起来太蠢了。

sentences.en: Why would you ever need that?
sentences.zh: 你为什么会需要它呢？

sentences.en: And admittedly, I think that's a very reasonable reaction to have to a function that literally just returns you what you pass into it.
sentences.zh: 诚然，我认为对于一个字面意思上只返回你传入内容的函数，这是一种非常合理的反应。

sentences.en: But if it's so useless, why did it show up in C++20?
sentences.zh: 但如果它这么没用，为什么它会出现在 C++20 中呢？

sentences.en: Well, you need it for composition, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你需要它来进行组合，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, if you're going to plug into some other higher order function.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你要接入其他高阶函数的话。

sentences.en: Yes, there are many higher order functions.
sentences.zh: 是的，有很多高阶函数。

sentences.en: And just in case there are some non-functional programmers that have, are not super familiar with the term, a higher order function is just a regular function, but it can
sentences.zh: 以防万一有些非函数式程序员对这个术语不太熟悉，高阶函数就是一个普通函数，但它可以

sentences.en: take a function as an argument or return a function.
sentences.zh: 接收一个函数作为参数，或者返回一个函数。

sentences.en: So it's just a function that takes other functions or returns functions.
sentences.zh: 所以它就是一个接收其他函数或返回函数的函数。

sentences.en: Great examples of these, sort of if you use sort of a little hand wavy, is like all of the std algorithMs. You know, std accumulate.
sentences.zh: 这些很好的例子，如果稍微笼统一点说，就像所有的 std 算法。你知道，std::accumulate。

sentences.en: Any algorithm that can be customized with a function object or a lambda, you can consider as kind of a higher order function.
sentences.zh: 任何可以用函数对象或 lambda 自定义的算法，你都可以认为是一种高阶函数。

sentences.en: It's not, you know, by the book definition because, you know, things decay to pointers and blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 它不是，你知道，按书本定义的，因为，你知道，东西会退化成指针之类的，巴拉巴拉。

sentences.en: But the equivalence of these in other languages, like Haskell and functional languages,
sentences.zh: 但在其他语言中，比如 Haskell 和函数式语言中，它们的等价物，

sentences.en: those are all higher order functions versus a function like, you know, plus that just adds two numbers together.
sentences.zh: 那些都是高阶函数，而像加法这种只把两个数字加在一起的函数，

sentences.en: That is not a higher order function.
sentences.zh: 那不是高阶函数。

sentences.en: It takes sort of data as arguments.
sentences.zh: 它接收的是数据作为参数。

sentences.en: So all of these combinators, so S, K, and I, I can describe, S is a little complicated, but I and K are super easy to describe.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些组合子，S、K 和 I，我可以描述一下，S 有点复杂，但 I 和 K 非常容易描述。

sentences.en: So I takes a single argument, it's a unary function, just returns you what you passed in.
sentences.zh: I 接收一个参数，它是一个一元函数，只是返回你传入的内容。

sentences.en: K takes, it's a binary function, takes two arguments and just returns you the first one.
sentences.zh: K 接收两个参数，它是一个二元函数，只是返回第一个参数。

sentences.en: So it throws away the second argument.
sentences.zh: 所以它丢弃了第二个参数。

sentences.en: Also seems a tiny bit useless, but these things become very important.
sentences.zh: 看起来也有一点点没用，但这些东西变得非常重要。

sentences.en: And S is what is known as the most powerful combinator of all.
sentences.zh: 而 S 被称为最强大的组合子。

sentences.en: In fact, Stephen Wolfram, for those of you that are following that guy,
sentences.zh: 事实上，斯蒂芬·沃尔夫勒姆，对于那些关注那个家伙的人来说，

sentences.en: Mathematica, he has the combinator challenge out right now.
sentences.zh: Mathematica 的作者，他现在正在进行组合子挑战。

sentences.en: He literally just launched it two weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 他就在两周前刚刚发起这个挑战。

sentences.en: And it's $20,000 to anybody that can show that the S combinator on its own is universally, is computationally universal, whatever that means.
sentences.zh: 任何能证明 S 组合子本身在计算上是通用的（无论这意味着什么）的人，都能获得 2 万美元奖金。

sentences.en: I don't actually think, initially I thought that meant that like you, you know, that means Turing complete.
sentences.zh: 我其实不认为，最初我以为那意味着，你知道，那意味着图灵完备。

sentences.en: So S and K are shown to be Turing complete, just on their own.
sentences.zh: 所以 S 和 K 被证明是图灵完备的，仅凭它们自己。

sentences.en: I thought he was asking to just so that S is Turing complete, but I don't think computationally universal is the same as Turing complete.
sentences.zh: 我以为他只是要求证明 S 是图灵完备的，但我认为计算通用性和图灵完备并不一样。

sentences.en: But S, what S is, is it is a function that takes three arguments, basically a binary function, a unary function, and an argument.
sentences.zh: 但 S 是什么呢，它是一个接收三个参数的函数，基本上是一个二元函数、一个一元函数和一个参数。

sentences.en: And the composition pattern there is you take your argument, pass it to the unary function, and then you take the result of that evaluation, along with the original argument again,
sentences.zh: 它的组合模式是：你取你的参数，传给一元函数，然后取那个计算结果，连同原始参数一起，

sentences.en: and pass those as two arguments to the binary function.
sentences.zh: 把它们作为两个参数传给二元函数。

sentences.en: So that is a little bit of something to digest like mentally, but a really easy example is, which I think we've talked about this on the podcast before, is palindrome.
sentences.zh: 所以这在心理上有点难消化，但一个非常简单的例子，我想我们在播客里讨论过，就是回文。

sentences.en: So if you want to check, is this string or is this vector of numbers, is palindromic, is if you reverse it, is it the same thing?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想检查这个字符串或数字向量是否是回文，即如果你反转它，它是否相同？

sentences.en: So your unary function is reverse, and C++ literally stood reverse.
sentences.zh: 那么你的一元函数是 reverse，C++ 字面上的 std::reverse。

sentences.en: Your binary function is stood equal, checking to whether a string or a list are the same thing.
sentences.zh: 你的二元函数是 std::equal，检查字符串或列表是否相同。

sentences.en: And the composition pattern then is you reverse the string or the vector, and then you take that reverse string with your initial string, pass those
sentences.zh: 组合模式就是你反转字符串或向量，然后把那个反转后的字符串和你的初始字符串一起，传给

sentences.en: to stood equal, and if they're the same, you know that you have a palindrome.
sentences.zh: std::equal，如果它们相同，你就知道你有一个回文。

sentences.en: So that's a very, very simple example of where you can use the S combinator.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常、非常简单的例子，说明了你可以如何使用 S 组合子。

sentences.en: And very interestingly, in the J language, which is the second array programming language that Ken Iverson worked on after APL, two juxtaposed functions form the S combinator.
sentences.zh: 非常有趣的是，在 J 语言中，这是肯·艾弗森在 APL 之后开发的第二种数组编程语言，两个并置的函数就构成了 S 组合子。

sentences.en: And they call that a hook because of sort of the pattern, which I'm not going to get into.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为“钩子”（hook），因为某种模式，我这里就不细说了。

sentences.en: And that is different from APL, where two juxtaposed functions is the B combinator.
sentences.zh: 这与 APL 不同，在 APL 中，两个并置的函数是 B 组合子。

sentences.en: Okay, explain what you mean by juxtaposed.
sentences.zh: 好吧，解释一下你说的“并置”是什么意思。

sentences.en: Just like side by side.
sentences.zh: 就像并排放在一起。

sentences.en: So literally like in J, equal, stood equal, the equivalent of stood equal is a verb or a function called match, which is hyphen, colon.
sentences.zh: 所以在 J 语言里，字面上，equal，std::equal 的等价物是一个叫 match 的动词或函数，即连字符加冒号。

sentences.en: So in J they have digraphs, so two ASCII symbols.
sentences.zh: 所以在 J 中他们有双字符符号，即两个 ASCII 符号。

sentences.en: So the equivalent of stood equal is hyphen, colon.
sentences.zh: 所以 std::equal 的等价物是连字符加冒号。

sentences.en: And reverse is pipe, period.
sentences.zh: 而 reverse 是竖线加句点。

sentences.en: So when you put those next to each other with the binary function first, and the unary function second, literally
sentences.zh: 所以当你把它们放在一起，二元函数在前，一元函数在后，字面上

sentences.en: without doing anything else, that automatically forms an S combinator, which they call a hook.
sentences.zh: 不需要做任何其他事情，它就自动形成了一个 S 组合子，他们称之为“钩子”。

sentences.en: Whereas an APL, if you put two, if you put those same functions next to each other, it's not going
sentences.zh: 而在 APL 中，如果你把两个，如果你把同样的函数放在一起，它不会

sentences.en: to evaluate correctly because it forms the B combinator, which if you're a Haskell programmer is
sentences.zh: 正确求值，因为它形成了 B 组合子，如果你是 Haskell 程序员，它就是

sentences.en: just the dot composition operator, which is you take two unary functions, you first evaluate the first one, and then you take the result of that and pass it to the second function.
sentences.zh: 点组合运算符，即你取两个一元函数，先对第一个求值，然后取结果传给第二个函数。

sentences.en: So like very, if you want to add one to a number and then multiply it by two, you can do, you know, one plus X, and then your
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想给一个数字加 1，然后乘以 2，你可以做，你知道，1 + X，然后你的

sentences.en: second thing you do two times X, and you just evaluate those in order.
sentences.zh: 第二件事做 2 * X，你只是按顺序求值。

sentences.en: So it's very interesting that APL uses the B combinator for what they call two trains, which is just two juxtaposed functions, whereas in J they use the S combinator.
sentences.zh: 所以非常有趣的是，APL 使用 B 组合子来实现他们所谓的“二元列车”（two trains），也就是两个并置的函数，而在 J 中他们使用 S 组合子。

sentences.en: And super interestingly, so J was developed in the early 90s.
sentences.zh: 超级有趣的是，J 是在 90 年代初开发的。

sentences.en: There's a paper by Roger Hooey, who was the main implementer that worked with Ken Iverson on J that he published in 2006.
sentences.zh: 有一篇罗杰·惠写的论文，他是与肯·艾弗森一起开发 J 的主要实现者，他在 2006 年发表了这篇论文。

sentences.en: And he called it hook conjunctions question mark, and basically asserts that after 17 years of experience using the S combinator for two juxtaposed functions, he thinks
sentences.zh: 他称之为“钩子连接词？”（hook conjunctions?），基本上断言在 17 年使用 S 组合子作为两个并置函数之后，他认为

sentences.en: that that was a mistake.
sentences.zh: 那是一个错误。

sentences.en: Because in APL, they have the three train, and J also has this.
sentences.zh: 因为在 APL 中，他们有“三元列车”（three train），J 也有这个。

sentences.en: So that's when it's called a fork, or an S prime combinator.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的“叉子”（fork），或者 S 素组合子。

sentences.en: And it's very, very similar to the S combinator, but the S combinator takes a binary function, a unary function, and your argument.
sentences.zh: 它与 S 组合子非常、非常相似，但 S 组合子接收一个二元函数、一个一元函数和你的参数。

sentences.en: An S prime combinator takes one binary function and two unary functions.
sentences.zh: S 素组合子接收一个二元函数和两个一元函数。

sentences.en: And it has the exact same pattern, but where we passed the original argument as the second argument for the S combinator, you basically
sentences.zh: 它有完全相同的模式，但在 S 组合子中我们把原始参数作为第二个参数传递的地方，你基本上

sentences.en: have the initial argument, you apply the unary function, each unary function to that initial
sentences.zh: 有初始参数，你对该初始参数应用一元函数，每个一元函数，

sentences.en: argument, and then take the results of both of those and pass them to the binary function.
sentences.zh: 然后取这两个结果并把它们传给二元函数。

sentences.en: So in order to define reverse, or sorry, is palindrome using an S prime combinator, you just need to, for that second
sentences.zh: 所以为了定义 reverse，或者抱歉，使用 S 素组合子定义“是否回文”，你只需要，对于第二个

sentences.en: unary operation, use the I combinator, use the identity function.
sentences.zh: 一元操作，使用 I 组合子，使用恒等函数。

sentences.en: So just like pass along the original one.
sentences.zh: 所以就像把原始参数传下去一样。

sentences.en: And so basically, he was pointing out that this S prime combinator, it's the more general version of the S combinator.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，他指出这个 S 素组合子是 S 组合子的更通用版本。

sentences.en: So as soon as you have the S prime combinator, you can already spell the S combinator just with an extra one or two characters.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦你有了 S 素组合子，你就可以只用额外的一两个字符来拼出 S 组合子。

sentences.en: And so it's sort of a waste.
